flashcard_questions.q: What is the moment of a force?
flashcard_questions.a: The turning effect of a force around a pivot.

flashcard_questions.q: Which equation is used to calculate a moment?
flashcard_questions.a: Moment = force × distance from the pivot.

flashcard_questions.q: What is the unit of a moment?
Which distance must be used when calculating a moment?
flashcard_questions.a: The perpendicular distance from the pivot to the line of the force.

flashcard_questions.q: A 420 N child sits 1.6 m from a see-saw pivot. What is the moment?
What does the principle of moments state about a balanced object?
flashcard_questions.a: Total clockwise moments about the pivot equal total anticlockwise moments.

flashcard_questions.q: What is a lever in physics?
flashcard_questions.a: A rigid bar that turns around a pivot to multiply the effect of a force.

flashcard_questions.q: When a small gear drives a large gear, what happens to the large gear?
flashcard_questions.a: It turns more slowly but with a greater moment.

flashcard_questions.q: In which direction do two meshed gears turn?
flashcard_questions.a: In opposite directions to each other.

flashcard_questions.q: Which equation is used to calculate momentum?
What is the unit of momentum?
Why is momentum described as a vector quantity?
flashcard_questions.a: It has both size and direction.

flashcard_questions.q: Which equation links force, change in momentum and time?
How do crumple zones reduce the force on a car's occupants?
flashcard_questions.a: They extend the time of the impact, so the force is smaller.

flashcard_questions.q: Why does increasing the collision time reduce the peak force?
flashcard_questions.a: The change in momentum is fixed, so a longer time gives a smaller force.

notes: 15 cards: 3 equation cards (moment, momentum, force from momentum change) worded exactly as the lesson states them, 2 unit cards, 1 worked-value card (672 Nm), 4 term to definition, 3 why/what-happens-if, 2 gear behaviour.
